segments.text: Here at Innovative Laser and Design customers come to the shop and of course they want to
see what we're doing, their interests, and what we're doing and we're glad to show them.
The problem we have to have when we bring them out in our shop is we got to look out for them.
They're used to being in homes or offices or businesses and they're not used to walking out
in an industrial shop. So a lot of times when you have customers in a shop you got to look out for them.
On the opposite side of the laser there's a safety map. You can see it's rolling back and
forth and this whole gantry is sliding on this rail back and forth while it's moving around and
cutting service panels and air and stuff like that. You do have to get to those for maintenance
but you need these up because if you're coming through here you know what you're doing in here.
You can't accidentally just, oh I didn't know I got in here. This chain's up. This should
be a warning. The laser beam is generated in this cabinet, bounces off of series of mirrors
that are shaping and turning the beam anti-reflective and sending it down to the
stickers and stuff. If I take that off there's the laser beam. There could be a laser beam behind
it or a warning. If you're doing maintenance of course you know that the beam's not shooting
right out when you take it out. You should know how to do your maintenance.
We're just using, you take these off in spectrometers.
